title: Semaphore Labs - POC success criteria & evaluation scoping
next_steps: Redwood to share POC SOW draft and pricing sheet by 2026-03-24
Semaphore to provide 200 golden prompts + 50 regression cases by 2026-03-26
Schedule benchmark run (hosted staging) week of 2026-03-30, Redwood to provision test token and sample dataset
Security: Redwood to send SOC 2 + architecture whitepaper to Jordan by 2026-03-23
action_items: Maya Chen: Draft POC SOW with goals, success metrics, and timeline (due 2026-03-24)
Alex Duarte: Deliver golden prompts, negative examples, and acceptance rubric (due 2026-03-26)
Liam O'Connor: Prepare benchmark harness script and latency/throughput config (due 2026-03-29)
Jordan Lee: Confirm network constraints and KMS requirements for private deployment test (due 2026-03-25)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC focused on quality and performance for an internal question-answering workflow. Agreed success criteria (accuracy and hallucination thresholds, p95 latency < 350ms for single-turn queries under hosted mode), dataset and golden prompt deliverables, benchmark plan and timeline, and security review items.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone — thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes. Quick intros please?
[00:06] Alex Duarte (Semaphore): Alex here, head of ML. We own the ranking/QA infra.
[00:09] Nina Park (Product): Nina product, owning search features.
[00:12] Samir Patel (SRE): Samir, infra and load testing.
[00:14] Jordan Lee (Security): Jordan, security and compliance.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Great. Liam and Priya from my side — Liam, Priya say hi.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE): Hey all. We'll focus on the eval/bench pieces.
[00:24] Priya Rao (Redwood SE): Hi — I'll be supporting prompt design and scoring.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Goal for today: scope a POC that proves Redwood meets your accuracy and cost/latency needs for the question-answering workflow. We want to pin down success metrics, what you can provide (golden prompts, negative examples), concrete benchmarks, and timeline.
[00:42] Nina Park: Sounds good. Quick context: we run a customer support search and internal docs QA flow. Current stack is an in-house reranker + a homegrown LLM ensemble that is patchy and expensive. We want to replace the reranker/LLM step with something cheaper and reliable.
[00:56] Alex Duarte: Our targets: maintain or improve correctness, reduce hallucinations, and cut inference cost. We have spikes — about 600 qps peak across global endpoints but our QA pipeline batched queries pre- and post-processing.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Helpful. When you say 600 qps peak, is that concurrent single-turn queries or after batching?
[01:15] Alex Duarte: That's incoming queries, single-turn at front door. Post-aggregation we batch for embeddings but this particular LLM step is single-turn re-ranking/generation, so low latency matters.
[01:24] Liam O'Connor: Ok, latency sensitive then. For POC options we usually test in hosted infra first to measure baseline latency and quality, then repeat on Dedicated or Private if customers need VPC. What's your preference?
[01:37] Samir Patel: Initially hosted is fine to prove the model. We'll need a private test later to validate egress controls — but that can be phase two.
[01:44] Jordan Lee: Agreed — we'll want to see the architecture and KMS flow, and SOC 2 evidence before any private deployment.
[01:51] Maya Chen: Noted. Let's talk success criteria. Typical buckets: quality (precision/recall or rubric scoring), hallucination rate tolerance, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k queries. What are your thresholds?
[02:05] Nina Park: For quality, product cares about F1-ish metrics on entity extraction and answer correctness. We can score on a 0–3 rubric (0 wrong, 3 perfect). Acceptance is mean score >= 2.5 on golden set. Hallucination threshold should be < 3% on a fixed negative prompt set.
[02:21] Alex Duarte: Add regression constraints — no more than 5% drop vs our baseline on the golden set for recall.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: Great. For latency, do you need p95 or p99?
[02:31] Samir Patel: p95 is our main metric — aim p95 < 350ms for single-turn under the hosted POC with 50 concurrent workers. If we see big diffs we'll dial batch/quantization.
[02:43] Priya Rao: On the golden prompts: we recommend a mix of 200 core prompts — 150 positive/golden and 50 adversarial/regression. Include real user paraphrases + edge-case instructions. We'll help refine once you share initial set.
[02:58] Nina Park: We'll pull 200 seeded prompts from our logs and annotate. Expect them by end of week.
[03:04] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll need negative cases — hallucination triggers — can you include 50 cases where the correct answer is "no answer" or where the doc doesn't contain the info?
[03:12] Alex Duarte: Yes we'll include that. Also note our answers are often tabular; we need format checks — like enforcing JSON output or specific fields.
[03:20] Priya Rao: Format checks are straightforward. We'll add schema validation into the evaluation harness. Hallucination checks we treat as an explicit binary label, then penalize strongly in scoring.
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: Scoring approach suggestion: combine rubric score and hallucination penalty to compute a normalized quality score. Example: normalized_score = mean_rubric_score - 2 * hallucination_rate. We can iterate on weights. Does that align with your product metric?
[03:43] Nina Park: We like that but need to ensure we don't over-penalize short answers. Maybe weight relative to severity-of-hallucination. We'll start with your formula as baseline.
[03:52] Samir Patel: On workload sizing — we need the benchmark harness to simulate our pattern: 600 qps peak with diurnal spikes. For the POC, can we run a synthetic load of 200 qps sustained with bursts to 600 qps?
[04:04] Liam O'Connor: Yes. For initial POC hosted benchmarks we'll provision a harness that runs three phases: cold-run (low concurrency for correctness), steady-state 200 qps for 30 mins, and spike tests with bursts to 600 qps for 10 mins. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, error rates, and cost per token.
[04:22] Maya Chen: Important to capture sequence length distribution. What's your typical avg token input and generated tokens?
[04:27] Alex Duarte: Average prompt ~ 80 tokens, generation typically 120 tokens. We have a heavy tail for long threads but the QA step is usually short.
[04:35] Priya Rao: We'll set test sequences to those distributions. For batching behavior it's sensitive to model and quantization runner, so we'll record effective batching efficiency.
[04:43] Nina Park: On models: are you planning to test several sizes/quantization? We want to balance cost and accuracy.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: We'll include two model variants: a higher-capacity open model (baseline accuracy) and a quantized lower-cost variant (for cost/latency trade-offs). If you prefer, also a Redwood-verified model profile.
[04:59] Alex Duarte: Good — compare at least one high-accuracy and one cost-optimised variant.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Security questions: where are logs stored, how long, and do you support customer-managed keys for encryption? Also audit logs for prompts/outputs?
[05:12] Maya Chen: We support retention controls and can enable encryption-at-rest with customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted POC will have standard retention but we can enable redaction. We'll send SOC 2 report and an architecture whitepaper after this call.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: We also need a data flow diagram for the hosted test — curious about transient storage of prompts/outputs.
[05:31] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the security packet.
[05:33] Nina Park: Timeline — you'd said 4 weeks earlier. Break that down please.
[05:37] Liam O'Connor: Typical cadence: Week 0 (this week) finalize SOW and dataset; Week 1 configure staging and initial correctness runs on golden set; Week 2 run steady-state benchmarks and iterate on model selection; Week 3 run regression and final acceptance with sign-off. Can be compressed if deliverables come earlier.
[05:53] Alex Duarte: So we want SOW and costing by Wednesday — that works. If we provide prompts by Friday can we start correctness runs early next week?
[06:02] Priya Rao: Yes. We'll need at least 48 hours to ingest and validate prompt formats.
[06:07] Maya Chen: About acceptance gating: we'll require mean rubric >= 2.5 and hallucination < 3% AND p95 latency < 350ms on the specified concurrency. Also cost per 1k queries target to be below X — we can propose numbers in the SOW.
[06:21] Nina Park: For cost target, give us both hosted and a modeled dedicated estimate once you see the throughput numbers.
[06:28] Liam O'Connor: Will do. We'll include a cost model: cost per 1k queries and projected monthly spend at your traffic profile.
[06:34] Samir Patel: For the benchmark harness we'll need an API key and a separate test tenant or scoped token — don't use our prod keys.
[06:41] Maya Chen: We'll provide a dedicated test token and a small test tenant for the hosted POC.
[06:45] Alex Duarte: Are there specific metrics you capture for hallucination detection? Automatic checks are not perfect.
[06:50] Priya Rao: We run a two-step approach: schema validation + semantic hallucination classifier and then human labeling on a sampled subset. For the POC we'll sample 200 post-run responses for human review to validate automated labels.
[07:03] Nina Park: That sample size seems small given our variance — can we bump to 500 for final acceptance?
[07:08] Priya Rao: Yes, final acceptance we'll recommend 500 human-validated samples. For interim runs 200 is quick feedback.
[07:16] Jordan Lee: On logging and PII — can Redwood redact PII before storing outputs when running hosted?
[07:21] Maya Chen: We can perform token-level redaction for sensitive patterns prior to persistent storage. We'll outline the redaction options in the security pack.
[07:30] Alex Duarte: Any pitfalls you've seen in similar POCs?
[07:33] Liam O'Connor: Two main pitfalls: 1) golden set mismatch — customers bring prompts that are unrepresentative (too sanitized). We encourage sampling real logs for diversity. 2) conflating cost optimization too early — test accuracy first, then explore quantized variants.
[07:48] Maya Chen: We'll help validate the golden set and propose augmentations.
[07:51] Nina Park: For regression tests, we need a CI-like harness that re-runs the golden and negative sets whenever model or infra changes. Is that part of the POC?
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: We can include a basic regression harness in the POC. If you want a long-term CI integration we can size that as an add-on.
[08:07] Samir Patel: Ops question — how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? Because our workload spikes unpredictably.
[08:13] Maya Chen: Hosted has burst capacity and autoscaling; we can configure reserves for predictable throughput. For Dedicated we provision capacity according to a commit. We'll model both in the cost appendix.
[08:24] Alex Duarte: Ok. Anything else on acceptance criteria?
[08:27] Nina Park: One more: format enforcement for JSON output — we need validators and structured fields exact match for downstream parsers.
[08:33] Priya Rao: We'll include a schema validator and add format checks to scoring (deduct if invalid JSON or missing required fields).
[08:40] Maya Chen: Recap: deliverables you provide = 200 golden prompts with labels + 50 adversarial/negative cases, sample token length distribution, and production traffic pattern. Redwood deliverables = SOW + pricing by 2026-03-24, security packet by 2026-03-23, staging tenant and test token, benchmark harness and initial runs next week. Acceptance criteria documented and gating as discussed.
[09:02] Alex Duarte: That matches. Quick question on competitors — we are demoing folks from Anthropic and an internal OpenAI experiment. How do you usually compare?
[09:12] Liam O'Connor: We'll include comparative baseline runs if you want; we can either use public model APIs or your artifacts. Note public benchmarking has rate-limits and noise; we recommend focusing on your baseline model provided or a previously recorded baseline.
[09:26] Nina Park: Fine. We'll provide baseline outputs for comparison.
[09:29] Jordan Lee: Last security note: we need an NDA in place?
[09:33] Maya Chen: We have a mutual NDA template; legal can exchange today. I'll include it with the SOW.
[09:38] Alex Duarte: Great. Any blockers on Redwood's side to start next week?
[09:41] Priya Rao: Need the prompts and a small schema of expected outputs. Also confirmation on which model variant you'd like us to run as priority.
[09:49] Alex Duarte: We'll send prompts and baseline by Friday. Model priority: accuracy-first then cost variant.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Solid. We'll send SOW and security docs Wednesday. Schedule benchmark run for week of 2026-03-30; we'll send calendar invites.
[10:02] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[10:04] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the packet.
[10:08] [call ends]
